exposure: subjective perception of birth as traumatic
cohort: The cohort consisted of 1064 mothers 6 to 12 weeks postpartum from Central-Eastern European countries (Poland, Slovakia, and Lithuania).
finding: The prevalence of clinical CB-PTSD ranged from 1.8% to 6.1% (3.4% for the total population), with common predictors including lower income, emergency caesarean section, postpartum depression, current psychiatric diagnosis, subjective perception of birth as traumatic, and lower birth satisfaction.
mod_finding: An emergency caesarean section, when compared to vaginal birth, was identified as a significant predictor of CB-PTSD symptom severity.
